mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy stance, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS declines (FEDFUNDS(t-1mo) < FEDFUNDS(t-2mo)), S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2 percentage points over one month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE rises >0.2pp in 1 month, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline (HOUST(t-1mo) < HOUST(t-2mo) and RSAFS(t-1mo) < RSAFS(t-2mo)), S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In supply shock regimes (industrial production decline), reduced manufacturing output signals economic disruption, increasing uncertainty and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO declines (INDPRO(t-1mo) < INDPRO(t-2mo)), S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, supporting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST rises (HOUST(t-1mo) > HOUST(t-2mo)), S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over one month signals potential monetary tightening, increasing real interest rates and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL rises >0.3pp in 1 month, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates labor market weakness from surging labor force participation, triggering economic uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS rises (PAYEMS(t-1mo) > PAYEMS(t-2mo)) and UNRATE rises (UNRATE(t-1mo) > UNRATE(t-2mo)), S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals aggressive monetary tightening, increasing real interest rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises (FEDFUNDS(t-1mo) > FEDFUNDS(t-2mo)), S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of cases, or Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is <0.03.
